chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When I intend to gather for a Muslim the good of this world and the Hereafter, I grant him a submissive heart, a tongue engaged in remembrance, a body patient in affliction, and a believing wife who delights him when he looks at her and who protects him when he is absent from her, in regard to herself and his wealth.'

key_terms.الْبَلَاءِ: Affliction, tribulation, divine trial — encompasses illness, loss, hardship
key_terms.تَسُرُّهُ: Delights him, brings him joy and happiness
key_terms.خَاشِعاً: Submissive, humble before God — connotes the heart's complete spiritual attentiveness
key_terms.ذَاكِراً: Engaged in dhikr (remembrance of God) — constant glorification and mention of the Divine
key_terms.صَابِراً: Patient, enduring — sabr is an active virtue involving steadfast acceptance

ai.seo_question: What are the four gifts God grants to a Muslim to give them the good of this world and the next?
ai.summary: This is a divine hadith (hadith qudsi) transmitted through Imam al-Baqir and the Prophet, in which God describes the four gifts He grants to a Muslim whom He wishes to bless with the good of both worlds: a spiritually receptive heart, a tongue constantly engaged in dhikr, a body that endures hardship with patience, and a righteous believing wife who brings joy to her husband's presence and faithfully guards his honor and property in his absence. The hadith appears in the chapter on the virtues of a compatible righteous wife, highlighting the spiritual and practical dimensions of a good marriage.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya Al Ijaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said Whenever I<sup>azwj</sup> Intend to Gather for the Muslim goodness of the world and the Hereafter, I<sup>azwj</sup> Make for him a devout heart, and a tongue of remembrance, and a body patient upon the affliction, and a Believing wife who delights him whenever he looks at her and she preserves him (his interests) whenever he is absent from her, with regards to herself and his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah al-‘Ijliy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, “When I want to bring together for a Muslim the goodness of this and the next life, I place in him a heart that shows reverence (to Me), a tongue that speaks (of Me), a body that bears patience in hardships and a believing wife who gives him joy when he looks to her and who protects his interest in his absence.’”
